narrativeReportMd:
# Extension R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Extension` has a local hard instance-breaking change: R4 `valueContributor` extension instances are no longer valid against the R6 base `Extension.value[x]` type list. R6 also adds six new `value[x]` choices that are valid in R6 but not natively representable in R4.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 and R6 core `StructureDefinition-Extension.json` files, package indexes, package metadata, the batch manifest, and selected datatype definitions needed to interpret the changed `value[x]` choices. The R6 counterpart is the same canonical artifact, not a renamed or split artifact. Inherited `Element`/`DataType` changes and the broader base hierarchy shift are recorded as out of scope for local findings.

## Main migration themes
The important migration work is concentrated in `Extension.value[x]`. Forward migration must detect and remediate R4 extensions that use `valueContributor`. Downgrade or round-trip tooling must handle R6-only values such as `valueCodeableReference`, `valueRatioRange`, and `valueInteger64` without silently dropping information. Summary serialization behavior also changes because `Extension.url` and `Extension.value[x]` are now marked summary elements.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the removal of `Contributor` from the extension value choice set. The second high-impact issue is R6-to-R4 representability for newly added value choices. Both affect strict validators, generated choice-type classes, and cross-version transforms.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for mapping old `valueContributor` content because the inspected package files do not provide an official ConceptMap or narrative migration rule. Human review is also needed when downgrading R6-only complex values to R4 because several are structurally richer than any single R4 extension value type.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Adding new R6 datatypes to `Extension.value[x]` is probably justified to keep extensions aligned with the R6 datatype inventory. Removing `Contributor` is a direct break for existing instances; a less disruptive approach would have been to keep it deprecated or provide an explicit cross-version mapping, but that depends on the fate of the `Contributor` datatype itself.

## Follow-up analysis
The `DataType` and `Element` reports should own the global hierarchy and inherited-element implications. A separate `Contributor` report should assess the removed datatype and any official R6 replacement strategy.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 keeps the same `Extension` artifact but changes the `value[x]` choice domain. The top concerns are removal of R4 `valueContributor`, addition of R6-only value choices that cannot be represented in base R4, and changed summary flags for `url`/`value[x]`. The main uncertainty is the absence of official migration guidance for `Contributor`.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration work should focus on the polymorphic `Extension.value[x]` surface. R4-to-R6 conversion needs a policy for `valueContributor`. R6-to-R4 conversion needs explicit downgrade behavior for `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, `RatioRange`, `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, and `VirtualServiceDetail`; lossless conversion may require cross-version extensions or preserving raw R6 payloads. Runtime stacks with generated choice enums or hand-coded `value[x]` switch statements should be regenerated and tested.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the structural deltas because they are directly visible in the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions and corroborated by package indexes. Confidence is lower for intent and best migration mapping because no official diff, Jira rationale, or ConceptMap for `Contributor` replacement was inspected.

findings.title: Extension.value[x] no longer permits Contributor

oldState.summary: R4 allowed `Contributor` as one of the `Extension.value[x]` choice types.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, an extension instance could use the JSON property `valueContributor` when the extension definition selected the `Contributor` datatype.

newState.summary: R6 removes `Contributor` from the allowed `Extension.value[x]` choice types, and the R6 core package does not include `StructureDefinition-Contributor.json`.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the base `Extension` type list no longer permits a `Contributor` value. An instance containing `valueContributor` is outside the R6 `Extension.value[x]` choice domain.

facts.note: The R4 type list includes `Contributor`; the R6 type list does not.
This supports treating `valueContributor` as removed rather than merely omitted from Extension by mistake.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id and path, `Extension.value[x]`, exists in both versions with unchanged cardinality. The only relevant local change for this finding is the choice-type list.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break. An R4 instance fragment containing `valueContributor` can satisfy the R4 base `Extension.value[x]` type list but will not satisfy the R6 base type list. Strict R6 parsers and generated models that enumerate permitted `value[x]` properties are expected to reject or fail to bind `valueContributor`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The removed datatype is mainly contributor/provenance-like knowledge-asset metadata. Loss or rejection can matter for governance and attribution, but no direct clinical-safety risk was identified from the base StructureDefinition alone.

justification.inferredGoal: Align `Extension.value[x]` with the R6 datatype inventory after `Contributor` was removed from the core package.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `Contributor` as a deprecated legacy R6 datatype and keep `valueContributor` in `Extension.value[x]`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local Extension goal appears to be consistency with the R6 datatype inventory after `Contributor` was removed from core. Given that R6 no longer carries a `Contributor` StructureDefinition, removing it from the universal extension value choice list is probably justified for Extension itself. The broader justification still depends on the datatype-retirement decision, but the less-breaking path has material model and implementation debt.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best backward-compatible base-design alternative is not conversion tooling or an R4 backport extension; it would require R6 itself to retain `Contributor` as a deprecated legacy datatype and keep `valueContributor` valid. That would preserve old R4 extension instances, but it only partially meets the R6 cleanup goal because every conformant R6 validator, schema, and code generator would still need to understand a datatype the rest of R6 is trying to remove.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve R4 instances but require R6 to keep an otherwise removed core datatype in validators, schemas, and generated models.

evidence.detail: R4 `Extension.value[x]` includes `Contributor` in its type list.
The R4 core package defines `Contributor` as a complex datatype with required `type` and `name` elements.
No R6 `StructureDefinition-Contributor.json` was present in the R6 package directory or index.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is illustrative rather than a complete resource. Its breaking feature is the `valueContributor` choice property, which was allowed by the R4 `Extension.value[x]` type list and is absent from R6.

findings.narrativeMd: `Extension.value[x]` is the generic carrier for simple extension values. Removing `Contributor` means an R4 extension definition or instance that used `valueContributor` cannot be carried forward as a conformant base R6 extension without changing representation. This can surprise implementers because the surrounding `Extension` artifact identity and cardinalities are otherwise stable.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid extension fragment with `valueContributor` becomes invalid against the R6 base `Extension` StructureDefinition because the choice element no longer admits that type. Runtime impact appears in validators, JSON/XML parsers that validate choice names, generated polymorphic accessors, and switch statements over permitted `value[x]` alternatives. This finding is not an R6-to-R4 representability issue because the type is absent in R6.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 data and extension definitions for `valueContributor`. If found, map to an R6-approved representation using official guidance if available; otherwise use a site-specific extension, an R6 datatype that captures the same facts, or a retained raw payload for audit. Migration is not guaranteed lossless because `Contributor.type`, `Contributor.name`, and `Contributor.contact` do not have a single base R6 `Extension.value[x]` replacement identified in the inspected inputs.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The breaking change was probably tied to removal of the `Contributor` datatype from the R6 core package. A backward-compatible alternative would have been to leave `Contributor` in `Extension.value[x]` as deprecated or to define a normative cross-version extension for it. That would reduce migration failures but keep legacy surface in the universal Extension value domain.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should confirm whether HL7 published a replacement or ConceptMap for R4 `Contributor`; none was found in the inspected local primary inputs.

findings.title: Extension.value[x] adds six R6-only value choices

oldState.summary: R4 did not permit `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, `RatioRange`, `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, or `VirtualServiceDetail` as extension values.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 extension values were limited to the R4 choice list and the R4 package did not contain these six datatypes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 expands the universal extension value domain to include new primitive and complex datatypes introduced after R4.

facts.note: These choice types are present in R6 and absent from R4.

facts.oldValue: No R4 StructureDefinition files for the six added R6 datatypes
facts.newValue: R6 StructureDefinition files exist for all six datatypes
facts.note: This confirms the issue is not merely an Extension list mismatch.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 elements match by id/path (`Extension.value[x]`) and unchanged cardinality; the delta is an additive choice-type expansion.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a forward validation break for existing R4 instances because adding choices widens the R6 domain. It is high impact for downgrade, round-trip, and mixed-version runtimes: a valid R6 extension can contain a `valueCodeableReference`, `valueRatioRange`, `valueAvailability`, `valueExtendedContactDetail`, `valueVirtualServiceDetail`, or `valueInteger64` that has no native R4 `Extension.value[x]` representation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If downgrade tooling drops or flattens these values, extension data may be lost. The risk depends on the extension URL and business meaning of the value.

justification.inferredGoal: Keep the base Extension value domain aligned with the R6 datatype inventory so extensions can carry newly introduced datatypes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 preserving alternative is needed because adding value choices widens R6 and preserves R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing `Extension.value[x]` to use datatypes introduced in R6 is a reasonable base R6 goal, and it does not make existing R4 extension instances invalid. The impact is a downgrade and mixed-version representability issue: R4 systems do not have native choice names or datatype definitions for the added R6 values.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This finding is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue under the calibration rules. Preventing R6 extensions from using R6 datatypes would avoid some R6-to-R4 downgrade work, but it would fail the R6 expressivity goal. Cross-version extensions, raw preservation, or per-datatype mappings are useful mitigations for R4 consumers, not backward-compatible base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 downgrade mappings may be needed, but those are migration mitigations rather than less-breaking base R6 alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 `Extension.value[x]` includes all six added types.
evidence.quote: integer64, CodeableReference, RatioRange, Availability, ExtendedContactDetail, VirtualServiceDetail

evidence.detail: The R6 package contains StructureDefinitions for all six newly allowed datatypes.
The R4 package does not contain StructureDefinitions for the six newly allowed R6 datatypes.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows one possible nested-extension surrogate for an R6 `CodeableReference.concept`. It is not a universal mapping and would need to be tied to a defined extension URL and migration policy.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 broadens the extension value choice list with datatypes that R4 does not know. This is useful for R6 authors but creates a cross-version boundary: older validators and generated models commonly implement `Extension.value[x]` as a closed set of allowed properties, so R6-only choice names can fail to parse or be dropped in R4-facing systems.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid merely because these choices were added. The risk is in the other direction: an R6-valid extension using one of the added choices is not a base R4 extension value. Strict R4 validators should reject the unknown choice property, and R4 code generators will not expose typed accessors for it.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Downgrade transforms should explicitly detect `valueInteger64`, `valueCodeableReference`, `valueRatioRange`, `valueAvailability`, `valueExtendedContactDetail`, and `valueVirtualServiceDetail`. If the business meaning must be preserved, use an extension-specific R4 representation, nested extensions, a raw-payload preservation strategy, or manual review. Do not silently coerce `integer64` into R4 `integer` because range and JSON representation constraints can differ.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The widening itself is probably justified: R6 extensions need to carry R6 datatypes. The backward-compatible path for mixed-version ecosystems is a published downgrade convention, not preventing R6 from using its own datatypes. Without such conventions, each extension URL needs case-by-case mapping.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact prevalence depends on R6 extension definitions that choose these new value types. The base `Extension` StructureDefinition establishes possibility, not frequency.

findings.title: Extension.url and Extension.value[x] are now summary elements

oldState.summary: R4 snapshot marks both `Extension.url` and `Extension.value[x]` as `isSummary: false`.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the local extension URL and value were not part of the base summary element set.

newState.summary: R6 snapshot marks both `Extension.url` and `Extension.value[x]` as `isSummary: true`.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the defining URL and value of an extension are included in summary handling metadata.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The elements match by unchanged ids and paths; only the summary flags changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Instance validity is unchanged, but summary flags can influence `_summary` responses, generated summary views, serializer filters, and data-minimization assumptions. R6 systems may include extension URLs and values where R4 summary-oriented code did not expect them.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main concern is privacy, payload-size, or client behavior when extension values appear in summary contexts. The base StructureDefinition does not identify a specific clinical safety hazard.

justification.inferredGoal: Make summary representations of extensions meaningful by including the extension URL and value.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the base `isSummary` flags false and rely on explicit `_elements`, profiles, or server policy to include extension URL and value.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: an extension summary is difficult to interpret without both the `url` that identifies it and the value it carries. The change can alter runtime summary output, but it does not invalidate instances. Because the less-breaking option materially weakens generic summary usefulness and shifts behavior to profile or server-specific policy, the break is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have left both summary flags false and documented that servers may include extension details only through explicit element selection, profiles, or local summary policy. That would reduce surprises for R4-oriented summary clients, but it only partially meets the R6 goal because generic `_summary` handling would still tend to expose extensions without enough information to interpret them, or omit them entirely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves R4-like summary payloads but leaves generic R6 summaries less self-describing and increases implementation variation.

examples.examplesMd: No instance content becomes invalid. The practical example is a server or serializer using StructureDefinition summary flags to decide whether `url` and `value[x]` appear in summary views.

findings.narrativeMd: The summary flag change is an additive runtime/serialization change rather than an instance validation break. It matters because extension content is often sensitive or semantically important, and generic FHIR infrastructure may use `isSummary` to shape partial responses or generated DTOs.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances remain R6-valid with respect to these flags. Valid R6 extension instances are still structurally representable in R4 unless they also use R6-only value types. The compatibility risk is behavioral: summary-mode serializers and clients can see different payloads even when the underlying instance is unchanged.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review code paths that use StructureDefinition `isSummary` metadata, especially `_summary=true`, summary DTOs, caching, privacy filtering, and generated serializers. Add tests showing whether extension `url` and value appear in summary outputs in both R4 and R6 modes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been avoided by leaving the flags false, but that would make summary extensions less useful because the value cannot be interpreted safely without the URL. Implementers that require R4-like summary behavior can still filter extension details explicitly.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, status, and abstract flag are stable; the package index confirms the R6 counterpart is `StructureDefinition-Extension.json`. The `baseDefinition` change to `DataType` is acknowledged but scoped to the global datatype hierarchy follow-up rather than counted as a local finding.

The local root, `Extension.url`, and `Extension.value[x]` elements are present in both versions with the same ids and paths. The inherited `Extension.id` and `Extension.extension` snapshot elements also remain present.
`Extension.value[x]` continues to include `Reference` with no local targetProfile restriction in either version.
The inspected local `Extension` elements do not introduce terminology bindings. Binding changes inside removed or added datatypes are delegated to those datatype reports.

The local `ext-1` invariant remains an error with the same FHIRPath expression, `extension.exists() != value.exists()`. R6 drops XPath metadata and moves condition pointers in the snapshot, but no material validation-semantics change was found for Extension itself.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value constraints were found on the local Extension elements in either version.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit changes were found on `Extension.url` or `Extension.value[x]`.
`isModifier` remains false for the root and local elements inspected.
The inherited `Extension.extension` slicing remains open and discriminated by `url`; no local slicing change was found.

No local SHALL-level semantic text change was found. The top-level description loses the phrase `Base StructureDefinition for`, and the inherited extension definition has minor wording/spelling differences, but these did not change computable conformance in the inspected StructureDefinitions.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: ext-1 validation expression is stable but metadata placement changed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The computable FHIRPath expression for `ext-1` remains `extension.exists() != value.exists()`, so the core rule that an extension has either nested extensions or a value, but not both, is unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that rely on XPath metadata or on which child element lists a `condition` may need regression tests, because R6 omits XPath metadata and records `condition: ["ext-1"]` on `Extension.value[x]`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds StructureDefinition type-characteristics metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds the top-level extension `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` with value `can-bind`. This is StructureDefinition metadata and does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or conformance tooling that consume StructureDefinition metadata may expose new capabilities for binding extensions, but no local element binding was added to the base Extension elements.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Minor descriptive text and publisher metadata changed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The inspected text changes do not alter cardinality, type domain beyond the findings above, constraints, modifier flags, or bindings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and generated descriptions may differ, including the R6 top-level description and publisher/contact metadata.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Extension.baseDefinition` changes from `Element` to `DataType` in R6. Per scope, the runtime/code-generation impact of the global datatype hierarchy shift should be assessed in the `DataType` report.
Inherited `id`, `extension`, `ele-1`, and broad XPath/condition metadata behavior should be assessed on `Element` rather than duplicated as local Extension findings.

`Contributor` is removed from `Extension.value[x]` and absent from the R6 package. A dedicated datatype-level report should assess whether it was removed, renamed, merged, or replaced and identify official migration guidance.

analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Locate an official cross-version map or narrative migration rule for `Contributor` and update the migration guidance.
